verses.text: "So Bezalel, Oholiab, and every skilled person to whom the LORD has given wisdom and understanding to know how to do all the work of building the holy place, are to do the work just as the LORD has commanded."
Then Moses called Bezalel and Oholiab and every skilled person to whom the LORD had given wisdom, everyone whose heart moved him to come and do the work.
They received from Moses all the offerings the people of Israel had brought for the work of building the holy place. And the people kept bringing more gifts every morning.
So all the skilled workers who were doing the work on the holy place stopped what they were doing,
and said to Moses, "The people are bringing much more than enough for the work the LORD commanded us to do."
So Moses gave an order, and it was announced all through the camp: "No man or woman is to make anything more as an offering for the holy place." So the people were stopped from bringing more,
because what they already had was more than enough to do all the work.
All the skilled workers among them made the holy tent with ten curtains of fine twisted linen and blue, purple, and red yarn, with cherubim sewn into them by a skilled worker.
All the curtains were the same size, about twelve and a half metres long and almost two metres wide.
They joined five of the curtains together, and did the same with the other five.
They made loops of blue cloth along the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and the same on the end curtain in the second set.
They made fifty loops on the one curtain and fifty loops on the end curtain of the second set, with the loops facing each other.
Then they made fifty gold hooks and used them to join the two sets of curtains together, so that the holy tent was one whole.
They made curtains of goat hair to make a tent over the holy tent, eleven curtains in all.
All eleven curtains were the same size, about thirteen and a half metres long and almost two metres wide.
They joined five of the curtains together into one set, and the other six into another set.
They made fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in the second set.
They made fifty bronze hooks to join the tent together, so that it was one whole.
They made a covering for the tent out of ram skins dyed red, and over that a covering of fine leather.
They made upright frames of acacia wood for the holy tent.
Each frame was about four and a half metres long and seventy centimetres wide.
Each frame had two pegs to fit them together. They made all the frames of the holy tent in this way.
They made twenty frames for the south side of the holy tent.
They made forty silver bases to go under the twenty frames, two bases for each frame, one under each peg.
For the other side, the north side of the holy tent, they made twenty frames,
and forty silver bases, two under each frame.
They made six frames for the back of the holy tent, the west end.
They made two frames for the corners at the back of the holy tent.
At these two corners the frames were double from the bottom all the way to the top, held by a single ring. Both corners were made like this.
So there were eight frames and sixteen silver bases, two under each frame.
They also made crossbars of acacia wood: five for the frames on one side of the holy tent,
five for the frames on the other side, and five for the frames on the west side at the back.
They made the middle crossbar so that it went all the way from one end to the other, halfway up the frames.
They covered the frames with gold, and made gold rings to hold the crossbars. They covered the crossbars with gold too.
They made the curtain of blue, purple, and red yarn and fine twisted linen, with cherubim sewn into it by a skilled worker.
They made four posts of acacia wood for it and covered them with gold. They made gold hooks for them, and cast four silver bases for them.
For the entrance of the tent they made a screen of blue, purple, and red yarn and fine twisted linen, the work of someone who sews beautiful patterns.
They made five posts with hooks for the screen. They covered the tops of the posts and their bands with gold, and made their five bases of bronze.
